properties.name: ROOT CAUSE: the settling cue read a call made for nobody as a call from someone who is not the owner, so the owner working alone (and every --call) was told settling was a question for the owner
properties.statement: ROOT CAUSE (walked with the root-cause skill) 2026-10-29, reflow2 main af851306c (#813). 1 OBSERVED: through `--call` on a fresh store whose Project has NO OWNED_BY edge (get_node: 0 OWNED_BY), add_decision's loop_hint said "settling it is the owner's word, and this call was made for nobody who owns this design: it is a question for the owner, not your next call (ask_question puts it to them)"; with OWNED_BY who:ann, replace_text said the same. Expected, by the owner's rule: the person running reflow2 locally is the one who can give the word. Not affected: a call naming a caller (writes_for) on a no-owner design was offered set_decision_status. The v0.94.0 release agent reported the no-owner case; #814's summary row said "or anyone, where no owner is named". 2 PRECEDENT: search_design found only #813's own records. 3 CANDIDATES and the measurement that would refute each. (C1) call_can_give_the_owners_word returned false on an empty WRITES_FOR BEFORE reading owners, so "names no owner" rescued only a NAMED caller — refuted if serving_for(None) on a no-owner in-memory design offered set_decision_status: it did NOT (the new test a_local_call_made_for_nobody_is_offered_the_settling_call FAILED on af851306c at line 96), and serving_for(Some(who:ann)) on the same design passed. CONFIRMED. (C2) the release agent's store named an owner after all (an import, or a tool drawing OWNED_BY implicitly) — refuted: a fresh store with 0 OWNED_BY edges gave the question wording, and only the owned_by tool writes OWNED_BY. (C3, outside the component) the --call door loses WRITES_FOR (another task, no scope) — refuted as the explanation: --call has no way to name a caller at all (only --http-trusted-gateway, for HTTP), and the in-process test with no door reproduces the wording. (C4) the observation is wrong (a stale binary) — refuted: reproduced on a debug build of af851306c on ajs77. (C5) the build contradicts its own description — refuted: the code, the capability's description, the changelog fragment, the Verification and the test all say "a named caller"; only #813's PR body sentence ("only if that contributor owns the design, or the design names no owner") parses both ways, and #814's row took the looser reading. 4 CLASS: the owner check decided "who is calling" by itself instead of asking crate::caller::CallerRule, the one place that says how this engine knows its caller. Locally (CallerRule::Local) the caller's word is all there is and anyone who can call can already edit the store, so an unnamed caller is the person running reflow2; only on an engine served for others does an unnamed caller mean nobody who can sign. Absence of a name was read as a negative identity. 5 FIX (Anthony 2026-10-29, "Go with your recommendation and fix them first"): ReflowService::call_can_give_the_owners_word offers the cue UNLESS the caller is known (writes_for, or the gateway/bearer-named caller) and is not an owner; unnamed → offered locally, not offered when served_for_others(). Behind flo2.io's gateway every call is named, so nothing changes there (pinned by behind_a_trusted_gateway_only_the_named_owner_is_offered_the_settling_call, which passes both before and after). 6 NOT ESTABLISHED: the recall pilot's re-run, if run locally with no writes_for, will again be offered set_decision_status — the pilot's own 101-offers case — unless its harness names the agent's contributor as writes_for.
